SMTO-LLM-0044 — The model's tool instructions could be read two ways

GUID: e88a34d2-4bd4-4c6f-b465-cfb6e74ac715
Slug: ambiguous-tool-arguments
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model sent its tool instructions in pieces, and those pieces fit together into two different sets of details. SMTO didn't run the tool rather than guess which one the model meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait to see whether the Run continues. SMTO may ask the model once more by itself after a reply it can't use. The pieces may fit together one way on the model's next try.
  2. If the Run stopped, read its activity in the conversation to see which steps already finished, then ask the Agent to continue only the rest. The tool was not run, but steps before it already happened. Repeating them could do the same work twice.
  3. If it keeps happening, ask the person who runs the model server to check how it streams tool requests, or choose a different model in Settings › Setup › Model routing. This mix-up comes from how the model server sends tool details in pieces.

What success looks like

  • The Run continues past this step, and the Agent's next action appears in its activity.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the model server or manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Streamed tool-argument fragments reconstruct into two different valid JSON objects (joined incremental pieces versus the final cumulative piece), so no single argument set is identified.

What this means

  • Stream reconstruction yields competing valid argument objects from the same fragments; neither interpretation has authority merely because it was tried first. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Stream reconstruction yields competing valid argument objects from the same fragments; neither interpretation has authority merely because it was tried first.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether the serving stack mixes cumulative argument snapshots and incremental fragments; compare complete candidates without executing either.

How to fix it

  • Raised by reconstruct_arguments in src/agent_runtime/llm/openai_compat/response.py. Fix the provider's streaming tool parser so it sends argument text either as incremental deltas or as cumulative text, consistently; check the raw fragments in the trace and do not choose between the candidate objects.
  • Repair the provider tool parser so it returns exactly one argument representation. Do not choose between conflicting argument values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Streamed arguments reconstruct deterministically to one object matching the advertised schema.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
